Once upon a time, I played an alpha version of Left 4 Dead - one that didn't have anything more than the core identity established. The Survivors didn't have their personalities, the music wasn't in, the level design was missing the trademark signposting, and there were a few other rough edges here and there. It was just four idiots with guns against the mobs, and while it was fun, sometimes you just had to guess where you were supposed to go and occasionally you wound up getting mobbed to death in a corner.

Those memories are what The Anacrusis reminds me of.

I gave it a shot and thought "good Early Access effort, give it another six months to cook and it'll be in good shape." Then, to my shock, I discovered that it had launched [i]over a year ago[/i]. Where is the polish? Weapons feel week because there's barely any hit response, enemies are jittery and buggy, resources spawn in floors or walls, horde events aren't well conveyed, almost everything is brightly lit and objectives are poorly telegraphed so it's ridiculously difficult to tell what's important or why.

It's a good start, but it needs to be more than just a good start. "Left 4 Dead with more weapons and build perks" was already done by Back 4 Blood.
